the vendor ஔ keys (slots 7A 26 on IE, INSCRIPT, KANIAN, MONO, PHONET86, PHONETIC, ENG, TAMIL99, ...) type ஒ + ள; the Unicode composer writes ஒள (U+0B92 U+0BB3), not ஔ (U+0B94 = ஒ + ௗ), and the ஔ code A6 has no 7 answer. Derived: ஒ 4A + the ள glyph CD.

HYPHEN-MINUS U+002D has no Shree code: the - key (code 2D, on 23 keyboards) makes the Unicode composer write EN DASH U+2013 and the 7 composer the dash glyph 26 (truth: – = 26). Byte 2D itself is an EMPTY glyph (advance 5) in every SHREE-TAM7/TAM face, so passing - through as 2D prints nothing. 26 and AD draw the identical dash.
EM DASH: code 7B is answered only by the 7 composer (97); 97 draws the long dash in every face.
code DD is answered only by the 7 composer (24); 24 draws ÷.
the chart key (Ctrl+Shift+1 *) holds code DC, and the 7 composer writes 23 for it - but 23 draws ய் (the same outline as B4). The × glyph is 96 (fonts/symbols.png). Shree itself prints ய் for ×.
U+0B82: the 7 composer writes 54 (= the கூ glyph) for code 77 and nothing for code 20; no Tamil face has an anusvara glyph
code DB: the Unicode composer answers a space, the 7 composer 1E (no glyph); no Tamil face has a rupee glyph
code ED: the 7 composer writes 88, the ௳ glyph; no face has a double danda
codes 5C/7C: the 7 composer writes 09/0A, which have no glyph in any face

the 7 composer writes control bytes 06-1C for them (# 12, $ 13, < 14, > 15, @ 16, _ 18, [ 0B, ] 0C, { 1A, } 1B, “ 0D, ” 0E, \ 17, | 1C, ` 19, ^ 0F, & 06) - no glyph in any face; their own ASCII bytes are TAMIL glyphs in these fonts (23 ய், 24 ÷, 26 dash, 3C empty/absent, 3E ।, 40 ே, 5B ங், 5C ச, 5D சி, 5E சீ, 5F சு, 60 சூ, 7B நி, 7C ந, 7D நீ, 7E நு). Nothing a table writes shows the symbol in a Shree Tamil font.

not a gap but a policy: bytes 30-39 draw WESTERN digits; Shree's Unicode composer writes Tamil digits U+0BE6-0BEF for the same keys (truth). ASCII digits 0-9 have no separate Shree code and pass through to the same bytes 30-39.
